name: recvmsg
synopsis: ssize_t recvmsg(int sockfd, struct msghdr *msg, int flags);
description: The recvmsg() system call is used to receive messages from a socket, supporting both connectionless and connection-oriented sockets. It utilizes a msghdr structure to handle data buffers, ancillary data, and flags for advanced options.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the socket from which to receive messages.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Pointer to a msghdr structure that specifies buffers for data, ancillary data, and other options.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags that modify the behavior of the call, such as MSG_DONTWAIT or MSG_OOB.

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes received.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error.

errors.description: The socket is marked nonblocking and the receive operation would block, or a receive timeout had been set.
The argument sockfd is an invalid file descriptor.
A remote host refused to allow the network connection.
The receive buffer pointer(s) point outside the process’s address space.
The receive was interrupted by delivery of a signal before any data was available.
Could not allocate memory for recvmsg().
The socket is associated with a connection-oriented protocol and has not been connected.
The file descriptor sockfd does not refer to a socket.
